---8<--- FILE: CLAUDE.md ---8<---

# CLAUDE.md

**Claude, start here.** The canonical AI guide for this repository is [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) — read it first (bootstrap protocol, quick start, commands, conventions, guardrails). Then read [`TASKS.md`](TASKS.md) for the currently assigned task. Never skip `TASKS.md`.

TL;DR:

- **AgentHive** = multi-agent orchestration (1 Master Agent + 20 specialized agents), Python 3.10+, FastAPI + SQLAlchemy 2 async, SQLite/PostgreSQL, typer CLI.
- Works fully offline: the deterministic mock provider answers, and its output is always tagged `[MOCK]`.
- Setup & run: `pip install -r requirements.txt && python run.py "request"`.
- Host-chat mode (you are the provider): run with `--chat`, answer JSON files from `./host_requests/` into `./host_responses/` — see [`CHAT.md`](CHAT.md).
- Verify before delivering: `pytest -q` and `ruff check src tests`.
- Secrets only via `.env` (never commit them); agent file tools are sandboxed to `WORKSPACE_DIR` (`./workspace`).

---8<--- FILE: .github/copilot-instructions.md ---8<---

# Copilot instructions

**Start from [`AGENTS.md`](../../AGENTS.md)** — it is the canonical guide for AI agents in this repository (bootstrap protocol, quick start, commands, conventions, guardrails). Then read [`TASKS.md`](../../TASKS.md) for the currently assigned task before writing any code.

Core rules:

- **AgentHive** = multi-agent orchestration (1 Master Agent + 20 specialized agents), Python 3.10+, FastAPI + SQLAlchemy 2 async, SQLite/PostgreSQL.
- Runs fully offline via a deterministic mock provider; mock output is always tagged `[MOCK]` — never remove the tag.
- After changes: `pytest -q` and `ruff check src tests` must pass.
- Never commit secrets; providers are referenced by environment-variable *name* (e.g. `OPENAI_API_KEY`) and values live only in `.env` (git-ignored).
- `configs/system.yaml` is operator-owned: do not edit it unless the task explicitly asks.
- Agent file tools resolve strictly inside `WORKSPACE_DIR` (`./workspace`); never write outside it.

---8<--- FILE: AGENTS.md ---8<---

# AGENTS.md — AgentHive

> **Nota per il proprietario (IT):** questo è il punto d'ingresso ufficiale per qualsiasi chat IA o agente di coding (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, Cursor, Codex…). Flusso previsto: la chat legge questo file → legge `TASKS.md` → esegue il compito affidato. Per assegnare un compito: scrivilo in `TASKS.md` oppure apri una issue con il template "AI task". Il file è in inglese per coerenza con il resto della documentazione della repo; le chat IA lo leggono senza problemi.

This file is the canonical guide for **any AI assistant, chat or coding agent** working on this repository, following the [agents.md](https://agents.md) convention. It is referenced from `CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md` and `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, so it is the one file every AI tool reads first.

## 1. Bootstrap protocol — do this first, in order

1. **Read this file completely** before touching any code.
2. **Read [`TASKS.md`](TASKS.md)** — the official queue of assigned tasks. Take the first open task (highest priority first). If the queue is empty but the user gave you a task in the chat, treat the user's message as the task and append it to `TASKS.md` before starting work.
3. **Skim [`README.md`](README.md)** for the big picture. If you are a cloud or local AI chat working without a local clone, read [`AI_CONTEXT.md`](AI_CONTEXT.md) — the complete operational package (quick start, offline config, provider configs, universal rules). Open `docs/*.md` only for the area you are working on (index in section 10).
4. **Set up and verify the environment** (section 3): the system must run end-to-end in mock mode before you change anything. This proves your environment works and gives you a baseline.
5. **Execute the task** following the conventions (section 7) and guardrails (section 8).
6. **Close the loop**: run `pytest -q` and `ruff check src tests`, update the task status in `TASKS.md`, and report honestly what you did — including anything you did not finish.

## 2. What AgentHive is

AgentHive is a multi-agent orchestration system: **1 Master Agent + 20 specialized agents** that analyze a request, decompose it into a task DAG, collaborate through shared memory and a persistent message bus, and deliver a single quality-gated result.

Key facts an agent must know:

- **Language/stack:** Python 3.10+, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy 2 async, SQLite (default) or PostgreSQL, Pydantic settings, typer CLI.
- **Runs fully offline:** with no API key and no Ollama, a deterministic mock provider answers; its output is always tagged `[MOCK]` and never pretends to be real AI output.
- **Operating modes:** A (simple, 1 agent), C (adaptive, 2–10 agents), B (collective, all 20 agents); chosen by a complexity heuristic or forced with `--mode`.
- **Quality gate:** deliverables must score ≥ 0.7 (completeness, requirements coverage, static AST check of embedded Python, secret scan, leftover-marker detection); up to 2 revision rounds.
- **Database:** SQLite at `./data/agent_hive.db`, created automatically; PostgreSQL via `DATABASE_URL`.
- **No secrets in the repo:** providers are referenced by *environment variable name* in YAML (`api_key_env: OPENAI_API_KEY`); values live only in `.env` (git-ignored).

## 3. Quick start (30 seconds)

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt   # once
python run.py "your request"      # runs a mission, prints a Markdown report
```

The database is created automatically. With no API key configured, results are deterministic mock output tagged `[MOCK]`.

## 4. Commands

```bash
python run.py "request"                  # run a mission (Markdown report)
python run.py --mode B "request"         # force collective mode (all 20 agents)
python run.py --chat "request"           # host provider mode: YOU answer the agent calls
python run.py demo logistica             # built-in demo (logistics plan)
python run.py demo codice                # built-in demo (Python + pytest)
python -m agent_hive.cli diagnose        # environment diagnostics
python -m agent_hive.cli recover         # reset tasks orphaned by a crash
agent-hive init-db                       # create all DB tables (server path)
agent-hive start                         # FastAPI server on http://127.0.0.1:8000
agent-hive status                        # agent roster + task statistics
agent-hive agents                        # list agents, roles, provider chains

make test        # pytest -q
make lint        # ruff check src tests
make typecheck   # mypy src
```

Full CLI and REST examples: [`README.md`](README.md) and [`docs/api.md`](docs/api.md).

## 5. Host-chat mode — when YOU are the LLM provider

If the user runs `python run.py --chat "request"` (or the `host` provider is selected), AgentHive delegates the actual LLM calls to the chat AI hosting it:

1. AgentHive writes one JSON request file per agent call into `./host_requests/`.
2. You read each request file, produce the answer, and write `./host_responses/<same-id>.json` containing:
   ```json
   {"text": "<the agent's full answer>"}
   ```
3. AgentHive polls for responses, consumes the files (deletes them after reading) and completes the mission, printing a Markdown report.

You can answer requests in any order. Full protocol: [`CHAT.md`](CHAT.md).

## 6. Repository map

```text
agent-hive/
├── AGENTS.md               # this file — AI entry point
├── AI_CONTEXT.md           # complete operational package for AI chats
├── TASKS.md                # queue of assigned tasks (READ IT FIRST)
├── CHAT.md                 # host-chat provider protocol
├── llms.txt                # machine-readable index for LLMs
├── llms-full.txt           # full text of the AI entry documents
├── README.md               # full documentation
├── SUPPORT.md              # where to get help
├── run.py                  # one-command entry point
├── configs/
│   ├── system.yaml         # orchestration thresholds + quality settings (operator-owned)
│   ├── master.yaml         # Master Agent configuration & permissions
│   └── agents/*.yaml       # 20 agent definitions (YAML)
├── src/agent_hive/
│   ├── hive.py             # composition root (one Hive per process)
│   ├── cli.py              # typer CLI
│   ├── api/                # FastAPI app + schemas
│   ├── orchestrator/       # master.py, planner.py, quality.py
│   ├── agents/             # base.py, runtime.py, roles/ (20 role modules)
│   ├── tasks/              # manager.py (state machine), scheduler.py
│   ├── memory/             # 3-tier MemoryManager
│   ├── communication/      # persistent MessageBus
│   ├── providers/          # openai_compat / ollama / mock + factory
│   ├── tools/              # permission-checked registry + builtins
│   ├── config/             # settings (env) + YAML loader
│   ├── db/                 # SQLAlchemy 2 async models + engine
│   └── core/               # errors, events, ids, logging
├── docs/                   # reference documentation (see section 10)
├── scripts/                # install.sh, start.sh, diagnose.py, smoke_test.py
├── tests/                  # pytest suite (SQLite, mock mode)
├── data/                   # runtime DB (git-ignored)
└── workspace/              # agent file-tool sandbox (git-ignored)
```

## 7. Conventions

- **Python 3.10+** with type hints everywhere; async/await for I/O.
- **Lint:** ruff (`ruff check src tests` must pass). **Types:** mypy (`make typecheck`).
- **Tests:** pytest (`pytest -q`), SQLite + mock mode, no network needed.
- **Adding agents:** drop a YAML in `configs/agents/` and (optionally) a role class in `src/agent_hive/agents/roles/`; role classes are auto-discovered (see [`docs/extending.md`](docs/extending.md)).
- **Config ownership:** orchestration thresholds and quality settings live in `configs/system.yaml`; per-agent config in `configs/agents/*.yaml`.
- **Commits/PRs:** small and focused; describe *what* and *why*; update docs when behavior changes.

## 8. Guardrails — never do this

- **Never commit secrets**, `.env`, keys or tokens. Secrets are referenced by env-var *name* only; values live in `.env` (git-ignored).
- **Never edit `configs/system.yaml`** unless the task explicitly asks: it is operator-owned and read-only at runtime.
- **Never disable or bypass the quality gate**, the secret scan or the `[MOCK]` tagging.
- **Never present mock output as real AI output** — mock results are tagged `[MOCK]` by design; keep the tag.
- **Never write outside the sandbox:** agent file tools resolve strictly inside `WORKSPACE_DIR` (`./workspace` by default); escaping paths raise `AgentError`.
- **Never enable the `file`/`http` tool families** in configs unless the task explicitly requires it (`ENABLE_FILE_TOOLS` / `ENABLE_HTTP_TOOLS`).

## 9. Definition of done

A task is complete when **all** of these hold:

1. The acceptance criteria in the `TASKS.md` entry are met.
2. `pytest -q` passes and `ruff check src tests` is clean.
3. Documentation is updated if behavior or interfaces changed.
4. The task entry in `TASKS.md` is moved to "Compiti completati" with a short result summary.
5. Anything unfinished, skipped or assumed is stated explicitly in your final report.

| Document | Read it when... |

| [`docs/providers.md`](docs/providers.md) | You touch provider chains, the circuit breaker, add a provider, or need local/cloud provider configs |

# Coda dei compiti affidati — TASKS.md

**Come funziona.** Questo file è il canale ufficiale con cui l'utente affida compiti alle chat IA che lavorano su questa repository. Ogni chat IA o agente che apre questa repo DEVE:

1. leggere prima [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) (protocollo di bootstrap, comandi, convenzioni, regole di sicurezza);
2. leggere questo file e prendere il primo compito aperto (priorità più alta);
3. eseguire il compito seguendo le regole in `AGENTS.md`;
4. a fine lavoro, spostare il compito in "Compiti completati" con un breve resoconto.

**Per assegnare un compito:** copia il template qui sotto nella sezione "Compiti aperti", compilando tutti i campi. In alternativa puoi aprire una issue con il template "AI task" (`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/ai-task.md`): le chat IA con accesso a GitHub la vedranno allo stesso modo.

## Compiti aperti

### T-002 — Applicare la matrice CI OS x Python a `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
- **Stato:** todo
- **Priorità:** alta
- **Assegnato a:** owner (applicazione manuale) oppure una chat IA con permesso `workflows`
- **Descrizione:** sostituire il job `test` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` con la matrice completa `ubuntu-latest` / `windows-latest` / `macos-latest` x Python `3.10` / `3.11` / `3.12` (fail-fast: false) e aggiungere il job `typecheck` (`mypy src`). La specifica completa pronta da incollare è in `AI_CONTEXT.md`, sezione 12 ("Migliorie CI"); il job `lint` resta invariato.
- **Criteri di accettazione:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` contiene la matrice e il job `typecheck`; la run CI su `main` è verde su tutte le celle della matrice.
- **Vincoli:** non toccare altro; il job `lint` non cambia; nessuna modifica al codice sorgente.
- **Esito / note:** da compilare a fine lavoro.

---8<--- FILE: CHAT.md ---8<---

# Using AgentHive inside an AI chat

0. Install dependencies once: `pip install -r requirements.txt`.
1. Download/clone the repository.
2. Run `python run.py --chat "your request"`.
3. AgentHive writes one JSON file per agent call into `./host_requests/`.
4. Read each request file, produce the answer, and write a JSON file with the same id into `./host_responses/`:
   ```json
   {"text": "<the agent's full answer>"}
   ```
5. AgentHive polls for responses and completes the mission, printing a Markdown report.

Files are consumed (deleted) after reading. You can answer them in any order.

See also: [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) — the full bootstrap protocol for AI agents working on this repository — and [`TASKS.md`](TASKS.md) — the current queue of assigned tasks.

## 1. Quick Start universale

```bash
git clone https://github.com/rajuferr-sketch/agent-hive.git
cd agent-hive
python -m venv .venv
```

Linux/macOS/WSL:

```bash
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install --upgrade pip
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
```

Windows PowerShell:

```powershell
.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python -m pip install --upgrade pip
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
```

Verifica:

```bash
python scripts/diagnose.py
python run.py "Diagnose this repository"
pytest -q
python -m ruff check src tests
python -m mypy src
```

## 2. Configurazione locale minima

Copia il template:

```bash
cp .env.example .env
```

Windows:

```powershell
Copy-Item .env.example .env
```

Configurazione offline:

```dotenv
DATABASE_URL=sqlite+aiosqlite:///./data/agent_hive.db
ALLOW_MOCK=true
LOG_LEVEL=INFO
CONFIG_DIR=./configs
WORKSPACE_DIR=./workspace
MAX_CONCURRENCY=8
DEFAULT_TASK_TIMEOUT=120
DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES=2
API_HOST=127.0.0.1
API_PORT=8000
ENABLE_FILE_TOOLS=false
ENABLE_HTTP_TOOLS=false
```

## 7. Comandi CLI

```bash
python run.py "Write a haiku"
python run.py --mode A "Write a Python hello world"
python run.py --mode C "Build a REST API"
python run.py --mode B "Create a complete SaaS architecture"
python run.py --format json "Analyze the repository"
python run.py --chat "Answer using the host AI"
python run.py demo logistica
python run.py demo codice
```

Con pacchetto installato:

```bash
agent-hive diagnose
agent-hive init-db
agent-hive run "Create a REST API" --mode C --json
agent-hive agents
agent-hive status
agent-hive recover
agent-hive start --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000
```

## 10. Regole universali per tutte le IA

- Non modificare segreti.
- Non modificare `.env`.
- Non modificare database SQLite.
- Non modificare workspace.
- Non modificare configurazioni fondamentali senza approvazione.
- Non aggiungere dipendenze senza motivo.
- Non assumere un sistema Unix su Windows.
- Non usare comandi Bash nei file Python.
- Non usare URL hardcoded nei provider.
- Non usare API key nei file versionati.
- Non usare network negli unit test.
- Non fare commit direttamente su `main`.
- Non fare merge di una PR senza test.
- Aggiornare test e documentazione insieme al codice.
- Usare type hints moderni compatibili con Python 3.10.
- Usare `pathlib` anziché concatenazioni manuali di percorsi.
- Usare logging anziché print nelle librerie.
- Usare eccezioni specifiche.
- Validare input API.
- Validare YAML.
- Validare JSON restituito dai modelli.
- Invalidare cache/circuit breaker dopo configurazioni nuove.
- Gestire cancellazione e timeout.
- Rendere tutte le operazioni ripetibili.
- Rendere gli script idempotenti.
- Registrare tutte le modifiche nello changelog.

> Nota operativa: la regola "Non fare commit direttamente su `main`" è vincolante per le IA e per i contributi esterni. L'owner può decidere quando applicarla a se stesso.

## 11. Struttura da preservare

```text
agent-hive/
├── .github/
├── configs/
│   ├── system.yaml
│   ├── master.yaml
│   └── agents/
├── docs/
├── scripts/
├── src/agent_hive/
│   ├── api/
│   ├── agents/
│   ├── communication/
│   ├── config/
│   ├── core/
│   ├── db/
│   ├── memory/
│   ├── orchestrator/
│   ├── providers/

├── docker-compose.yml
├── pyproject.toml
├── requirements.txt
├── requirements-dev.txt
├── AGENTS.md
└── README.md
```

### Migliorie CI

- **Matrice OS x Python (specifica pronta, da applicare manualmente):** sostituire `.github/workflows/ci.yml` con la configurazione qui sotto — job `lint` invariato, nuovo job `typecheck` (mypy), job `test` in matrice `ubuntu-latest` / `windows-latest` / `macos-latest` x Python `3.10` / `3.11` / `3.12` con fail-fast disattivato. Applicazione richiede un token con permesso `workflows` oppure l'intervento manuale dell'owner (tracciato come T-002 in [`TASKS.md`](TASKS.md)).

```yaml
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  lint:
    name: Lint (ruff)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
          cache: pip

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pip install -r requirements-dev.txt

      - name: Ruff check
        run: ruff check src tests

  typecheck:
    name: Typecheck (mypy)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
          cache: pip

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
          pip install -e ".[dev]"

      - name: MyPy
        run: mypy src

  test:
    name: Tests (${{ matrix.os }}, Python ${{ matrix.python-version }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, windows-latest, macos-latest]
        python-version: ["3.10", "3.11", "3.12"]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}
          cache: pip

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install -r requirements.txt -r requirements-dev.txt
          pip install -e ".[dev]"

      - name: Run test suite
        run: pytest -q
```

- Pianificate per una fase successiva (da applicare singolarmente e verificare in CI prima del merge): CodeQL, coverage, SBOM, secret scan, dependency review, Docker build, smoke test, test packaging, test PostgreSQL.

## 17. Prompt pronto da dare a qualunque IA

```text
Stai lavorando sul repository rajuferr-sketch/agent-hive.

Leggi AGENTS.md, README.md e pyproject.toml.
Non modificare segreti, .env, data/, workspace/ o configurazioni
fondamentali senza istruzioni esplicite.
Lavora su un nuovo branch.
Mantieni Python >=3.10 compatibile.
Mantieni compatibilità Linux, Windows, macOS e Docker.
Usa provider mock nei test.
Esegui prima i test esistenti.
Aggiungi test per ogni modifica.
Esegui python scripts/diagnose.py, pytest -q,
python -m ruff check src tests e python -m mypy src.
Mostrami il piano prima delle modifiche.
Crea il diff finale.
Non creare, modificare o esporre chiavi API.
Apri una pull request solo dopo che tutti i controlli passano.
```

## 18. Stato finale previsto

Una volta applicato questo pacchetto:

- compatibilità reale con modelli cloud e locali;
- GitHub Actions multipiattaforma;
- Docker e PostgreSQL verificati;
- provider IA configurabili;
- API protetta;
- database migrabile;
- installazione locale ripetibile;
- istruzioni leggibili da ogni IA;
- codice testato prima del merge;
- release e SBOM;
- branch protetto;
- segreti fuori dal repository;
- documentazione completa;
- supporto Claude, ChatGPT, Z.AI/GLM, Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM e LiteLLM;
- contributi sicuri tramite PR;
- operazioni locali e cloud documentate;
- progetto pronto per uso personale, comunitario e commerciale.
